sources.fullCitation: B. Kaper and Walter Jurmann, Der glückliche Herr Fünf (Tonfilm): Schlagerheft containing “Tränen in der Geige” and “Schön ist das ganze Leben,” words by Fritz Rotter. Berlin: Edition Brüll, 1932. Registered in Hofmeisters Musikalisch-literarischer Monatsbericht 104, no. 11 (November 1932): 220. ANNO – Austrian Newspapers Online, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek.

sources.title: Der Kinematograph (Berlin), August 1932, p. 118
sources.shortCitation: Der Kinematograph, August 1932, p. 118 — Der glückliche Herr Fünf advertisement
sources.fullCitation: Advertisement, “Demnächst erscheint: Der glückliche Herr Fünf, nach dem Roman Herr Fünf von Alice Berend. Regie: Heinz Hilpert. Musik: Dr. Kaper und Walter Jurmann. In der Hauptrolle: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender. Produktion: Pax Film GmbH, Berlin SW 68.” Der Kinematograph (Berlin), August 1932, p. 118. Digitised issue at the Internet Archive. The film was released in 1933 as Ich will Dich Liebe lehren. Accessed 6 August 2026.

sources.fullCitation: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender, with the Marek Weber Orchestra conducted by Marek Weber. “Ich will dich Liebe lehren: Tranen in der Geige.” Music by Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann, words by Fritz Rotter. On Schlager und Filmmelodien von Walter Jurmann, Vol. 1 (Recordings 1930–1938). Jube Pops, released 5 February 2013; art track supplied to YouTube by Naxos Digital Services and published on the auto-generated artist channel on 11 February 2015. The reissue does not identify the original disc. Accessed 15 August 2026.

media.title: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender as Figaro — Ross Verlag postcard, c. 1928
media.altText: Photographic postcard portrait of the baritone Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender in costume as Figaro.
media.publicCaption: Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender as Figaro in Rossini's Il barbiere di Siviglia, on a signed Ross Verlag artist postcard of about 1928. He took the lead in Ich will Dich Liebe lehren, singing Tränen in der Geige and Schön ist das ganze Leben.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unknown; signed artist postcard, Ross Verlag, c. 1928; private collection, via Wikimedia Commons.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The Wikimedia Commons file records the postcard as published more than seventy years ago without a public claim of authorship, which places an anonymous work out of copyright in the European Union, and as published before 1 January 1931, which places it out of copyright in the United States. The photographer is not named on the card.

contributions.scopeNote: Recorded the song with the Marek Weber Orchestra; the recording is published on the Jube Pops compilation of Walter Jurmann's film songs. He also played the lead in Der glückliche Herr Fünf, the film the song comes from, as the trade advertisement announces.
